headline: Markets snap back hard from the AI sell-off, but conviction is fragile
body: Tuesday opens on the heels of one of the sharpest two-way swings the AI trade has seen this year. Chip and AI-infrastructure names were dumped hard last week, with Nvidia falling over 9% in a single session and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping roughly 12%, pulling the Nasdaq into correction territory on bubble-valuation worries. Monday reversed that violently: the Dow jumped over 1,100 points (+2.15%), the S&P 500 gained 2.35% in its best day since April, and the Nasdaq rose 2.74%, with falling oil prices (Brent down over 5%) and a retreating VIX (back near 20) helping the broader tape even as Nvidia itself lagged the rebound. That sequence — a violent drawdown followed by an equally violent snapback — looks less like a resolved correction than a market still searching for a stable read on AI valuations.

With Nvidia's next earnings print due November 17, the coming week is shaping up as a test of whether Monday's bounce reflects genuine dip-buying conviction or just a reflexive unwind of an oversold position. Retail-sentiment trackers didn't turn up a clear, current signal today, so this read leans on price action and positioning rather than social-media chatter. The split behavior so far — sharp snapbacks concentrated in the names that fell hardest, rather than a uniform rally — suggests traders are rotating within the AI trade and re-testing conviction level by level, not broadly re-risking across the market.
